paraphrase: Preservation of the body is hard even for gods, how much more for men on earth; when dharma is lost, rites are lost; without rites no yoga; without yoga no goal; without the goal no liberation.

paraphrase: The stability of the body is gained by the discipline of action (karmayoga), which is twofold: mercury and breath. 'Swooned, it removes disease; dead, it revives itself; bound, it gives the power of moving in the sky — mercury and breath, O Bhairavī.' Liberation is from knowledge, knowledge from holding the breath; the body is stable where mercury is lord in stabilizing it; soon the body becomes ageless and deathless (the second line of 1.21, on meditation of the mind and the yoga of mercury, is of uncertain sense and not paraphrased).

paraphrase: Until the descent of power (śaktipāta) and the cutting of the fetters, how can understanding of mercury arise? Rasa-knowledge is very hard for those whose minds are ruined by constant wine, meat and sexual rites; for those without the Kula teaching mercury does not succeed — they drink a mirage. Without eating the seed of Hara (mercury) how can there be liberation or preservation of the body? Deluded by Śiva's māyā, those addicted to wine and meat babble 'we are liberated, we shall go to Śiva's abode'; the whole world is coloured by partial knowledge. Practise constantly that knowledge of rasa by which one gains sky-going and Śivahood in one's own body.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: You are the mother of all beings and I the eternal father; the rasa born of our great union is called pārada because the best adepts proclaim it 'for the sake of others' (para-artha); this sūta is equal to me, born from my limbs; since it is the rasa of my body it is called rasa.

paraphrase: From seeing, touching, eating, remembering, worshipping and giving mercury a sixfold fruit is seen: the merit of seeing all the liṅgas on earth comes from seeing mercury; eaten it destroys the three sins, the three sufferings and the diseases of the three doṣas; remembering it frees from sins of former births; worship of the mercurial liṅga yields a crore-fold the fruit of worshipping thousands of self-born liṅgas.

paraphrase: The alchemy of the sky (khaga-vāda) is lowest, that of caves (bila-vāda) middling, that of mantra high, and the alchemy of mercury (rasavāda) highest; those who, knowing mantra and tantra, disparage the yoga of mercury go to hell, cutting off their store of merit. Rasa-knowledge is the supreme knowledge, giving enjoyment and liberation, to be given only to the qualified; success comes to the believer, not to one who says 'it is not'; the slanderer of rasa is reborn for countless births as dog, cat, donkey, crow, worm, cock and vulture, and whoever talks with or touches such slanderers suffers for a thousand births.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: First worship the guru with a pure inner self; when the guru is pleased the rays (of the teaching) grant the lineage-tradition (sampradāya). The fool who works without serving the guru finds his work fruitless as wealth found in a dream. This great tantra is most rare, to be kept secret, obtained through the guru's grace for the attainment of its fruit; having gained the rasa-works one should not become proud; permitted by the guru, having received the command, one should accomplish the Rasa-Bhairava.

paraphrase: Liberation at the falling of the body is meaningless: when the body falls even a donkey is freed; if liberation came from sexual excitement or from consuming bodily fluids, dogs and pigs would be liberated. In the six systems liberation is shown at the body's fall, but it is not perceived like a myrobalan in the hand; therefore one should protect the body with rasas and rasāyanas.
